transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-09 16:00 UTC
Duration: 78 minutes
Attendees: Elena, Marcus, Priya, Samir, Clara, Jade, Drew, Nora + all staff

Summary: quick launch of the Stability & Ops playbook, incident recap from late Oct, SLO changes, ops requirements for Dedicated and Private customers, hiring note, open Q&A.

[00:00] Elena (CEO): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I know it's a busy week so we really appreciate you carving out time. Long agenda but we want to get the playbook out and make sure folks feel comfortable with the runbooks.

[00:38] Marcus (CTO): I'll start with the incident recap, very brief. On 10/28 we had a P1 that hit our hosted API during a spike of long-context generation. Root cause was a combo of an unexpected KV-cash eviction pattern and a kernel fallback on some older GPU nodes.

[01:20] Drew (SRE): yeah, the KV cash - uh cash - sorry, KV cache - got trimmed by the compaction job that ran out of schedule. That made certain requests fall back to full model reloads and we saw tail latency blow out.

[02:05] Priya (VP Product): A few folks raised the question in slack about why Dedicated tenants saw different behavior. Short answer: Dedicated pools had a different eviction window and less aggressive compaction but also more headroom so impact was variable.

[02:48] Speaker 1 (unlabeled): Do we have telemetry we can point customers to? Some customers asked for more granular logs and the audit trail.

[03:15] Clara (VP Ops): We're shipping an observability dashboard that surfaces token-level latency, KV cache hit rates, and kernel-selection events. It's in beta for a small set of Console tenants next week. Link in the follow ups.

[03:58] Marcus: Important note: we are moving to explicit latency tiers in the SLOs. Hosted has default SLOs at p95/p99 latency, Dedicated customers can opt into stricter tail-latency SLOs and Private deployments will be allowed custom SLOs driven by on-prem capacity.

[04:38] Elena: This matters because product and sales need a single story about what good looks like. We don't want sales promising sub-50ms for workloads that are actually long-context with low quantization.

[05:10] Nora (Customer Success): Quick customer anecdote - one customer in finance asked for data residency + private inference and also wanted a weekly SLA report. We told them we're able to create a reporting bundle but need the playbook to standardize the process.

[05:42] Jade (Eng Manager): On the playbook: it's structured around triage, containment, root-cause, postmortem, and customer communication templates. There's also a short ops quiz to ensure folks read it. We tried to keep it short so it's actually consumed.

[06:18] Marcus: Technical items to highlight in playbook: circuit-breaker settings for heavy beams (long sequences), KV cache warmup guidance for model rollouts, and recommended quantization profiles for edge Dedicated hardware. Some of those terms may be slightly fuzzy in the docs - we'll refine.

[07:02] Samir (Head of Platform): I'll take responsibility for the runbooks for Dedicated and Private. The playbook will live in Confluence and we'll version it. For Private installs we also include a network checklist: firewall rules, KMS integration, and audit log export.

[07:40] Q: (someone in audience): will the playbook replace incident runbooks?

[07:55] Samir: No — think of it as the umbrella. Playbook = policy + templates. Runbooks = step-by-step ops commands and scripts. Both will cross-link.

[08:28] Drew: On-call changes - we reduced single-person blast radius by adding a backup pager on each team and moving to a 12-hour shift shadowing window for new on-call. Details in the policy doc.

[09:10] Priya: We'll also start tabletop exercises monthly, cross functional, to run through at least two P1 scenarios each quarter. Those should uncover gaps in playbooks and training.

[09:42] Elena: Hiring note - headcount freeze is eased for critical infra hires. We approved 6 new hires focused on SRE and performance engineering for Q1. We need to keep interviews tight and prioritize folks with production-inference backgrounds.

[10:15] Clara: Cost telemetry - Ops and Finance want per-tenant cost breakdown by token-class and model variant. We're shipping a first pass in Console that shows per-route token cost, kernel type, and percent of time spent on fallback kernels.

[10:52] Marcus: That will help with our Optimize recommendations — batching and cache suggestions tied to actual unit economics.

[11:22] Speaker 2: there was a question about encryption in Private - customers want HSM and double-encryption?

[11:38] Samir: We support KMS/HSM integrations already in Private. Double-encryption patterns add ops complexity; we'll document recommended architectures in the playbook.

[12:05] Audience noise / murmur

[12:30] Elena: Ok open Q&A, please put hands up or drop questions in the Q&A panel. We'll alternate between leadership and product.

[12:55] Question: "How does this change priority for product roadmaps?"

[13:10] Priya: short answer: it nudges us to prioritize reliability work and observability features that directly reduce operational toil. We'll re-scope a couple of small feature bets to make room.

[13:48] Marcus: And from infra, the big ticket is synthetic load testing and better kernel-selection telemetry. We want to be able to quickly reproduce the tail-latency behavior seen in production.

[14:25] Jade: For engineering managers: we'll require two on-call rotations for folks who are owners of model rollouts. It's to spread knowledge and avoid single points of failure during model switches.

[14:58] Question from Sales (Nora reading): "What's the comms plan to customers? Should AEs start sending heads-up?"

[15:15] Elena: AEs can send a short email template that Clara will provide — it's a heads-up about playbook, improved monitoring, and a link to sign up for the beta dashboards. We want to avoid alarming customers.

[15:45] Marcus: Important technical note—some naming in docs may be slightly off, for example 'Redwood Dedicate' shows up in a few drafts — we'll fix those. Also we sometimes see transcription recogs replace 'KV cache' with 'KV cash' in notes, so apologies in advance.

[16:10] Q: "How will we measure adoption of the playbook?"

[16:25] Clara: We'll track completion of the ops quiz, number of tabletop tests completed, percentage of runbooks linked to incidents, and a reduction in time-to-restore metrics. We'll publish a weekly adoption dashboard.

[17:00] Audience: (chat) thumbs up

[17:20] Marcus: On Dedicated SLAs - we will offer an optional Tail-Latency Guarantee add-on for certain customers. That will require contractual terms and a different capacity reservation model. Sales and Legal will coordinate.

[17:50] Elena: On the topic of pricing and cost controls: Optimize will surface economization suggestions — but customers must opt into caching and batching settings that may affect determinism of responses for some models.

[18:20] Priya: We'll include a short set of safe defaults in the playbook so teams and customers can pick a profile: low-latency, cost-saver, or deterministic. Each profile maps to batching and quantization params.

[18:50] Q: "Will teams be forced into new profiling?"

[19:05] Priya: No, it's opt-in for existing customers, mandatory for new Dedicated contracts after a grace period. We'll communicate timelines clearly.

[19:35] Drew: Ops checklist includes a quick health script to run post-deploy and a KV cache warmup step for model switches. It's a one-liner in our repo.

[20:00] Short pause, laughter, small cross talk

[20:20] Elena: Quick product demo from Priya on the Console adoption dashboard.

[20:32] Priya: (screen share described) Here's the weekly adoption view: playbook read rate, quiz completion, number of linked runbooks. There's also a list of recent incidents with flagged gaps. You can filter by model family and by region.

[21:10] Audience: (some questions about filter behavior)

[21:45] Priya: note: "model family" currently maps to our catalog names; some older names need re-mapping. We'll address in the next docs pass.

[22:10] Question: "Will Private customers get the same dashboard?"

[22:28] Clara: For Private we'll ship a local collector that pushes metrics to the customer's observability stack and an optional export to Console when permitted. Otherwise we'll provide the dashboard package they can host.

[22:58] Marcus: We also touched on regional fallbacks. Playbook clarifies fallback policies by region and model variant to avoid blackholing requests.

[23:30] Elena: Ok final segment: leadership three asks for the org. Marcus?

[23:42] Marcus: 1) read the playbook, 2) run the short ops quiz, 3) join one tabletop session.

[24:00] Priya: And product: prioritize the top two console features that reduce mean time to detect.

[24:12] Clara: Ops: sign up for the beta dashboards and start the synthetic load tests with Drew's jobs.

[24:32] Q&A continues for the next ~40 minutes with rotation of folks calling out clarifications, a few interruptions, and some transcription artifacts: names mis-heard, technical terms slightly off. Highlights: a Sales question about renewal timing for a big customer, an Engineering question about kernel selection heuristics, and a Compliance question about audit log retention for Private installs.

[45:12] Marcus (detailed): On kernel selection heuristics - we're adding a telemetry tag to every request that records fallback reason and chosen kernel. That will let us build a classifier to choose the best kernel for given shapes. Early rollout next sprint.

[55:03] Drew: Status update on synthetic jobs - first baseline run completed, saw 2% of requests hitting fallback paths at 99th percentile under current config. We'll iterate on cache warmup.

[62:40] Priya: On legal/commercial: Clara and legal are building a Tail-Latency Addendum template. We'll need sales to sign off on rollout plan.

[70:05] Elena: Closing notes - appreciate the hard work. This playbook is not a hammer, it's a shield for customers and for our teams. We'll take feedback and iterate fast.

[71:00] Final quick lightning round questions (audio overlap): Who owns the playbook? Samir. Who owns the quiz? Jade. Who schedules tabletop? Priya.

[72:12] Elena: Thanks everyone, recording will be posted. Please fill the short survey afterwards.

[72:40] End meeting
